rows.title: Murabahah Policy Document (BNM/RH/STD 028-4)
key_clauses: Institution must obtain ownership and assume ownership risk of the asset PRIOR to executing the murabahah contract, regardless of the customer's preceding purchase undertaking (read verbatim)
Covers murabahah to the purchase orderer (MPO) structure

rows.title: Kafalah Policy Document (revised 17 Apr 2017)
rows.effective: 1 January 2018 except Part E immediate (verified in text)
key_clauses: 8.1 kafalah = guarantor conjoins the guaranteed party in assuming the latter's specified liability
15.1 the guarantor MAY impose a fee for providing the kafalah service
15.2 fee may be an agreed fixed amount OR a percentage of the guaranteed amount
8.2 fee-paid kafalah cannot be dissolved without the guaranteed party's consent
rows.note: THE fee-permissibility position — contrast AAOIFI SS 5 restrictive stance; exactly the side-by-side the Kafalah demo showcases

rows.title: Shariah Governance Policy Document 2019
key_clauses: Applies to Islamic banks, takaful/retakaful operators, Islamic-window banks, prescribed DFIs
Shariah committee accountable for the quality, accuracy and soundness of its own decisions
rows.supersession_note: replaces BNM SGF 2010 regime — the tracker's BNM-SG-2019 deep note now has full text on disk

rows.title: Shariah Governance Framework for Local Banks (Feb 2020)
key_clauses: Art. 7: board forms the Shariah committee on nomination/remuneration committee recommendation
Independence invalidated if a member owns >=5% of bank stock (article enforced from 01/01/2023 — read verbatim)
Bank must establish a control mechanism ensuring Islamic operations comply with Shariah at all times

rows.title: Standard re. Shari'ah Governance for Islamic Financial Institutions
key_clauses: IFIs bound by resolutions, fatwas, regulations and standards issued by the Higher Shari'ah Authority (HSA)
Internal Shari'ah Supervision Committee (ISSC) required per institution; bilingual standard (AR/EN)
rows.note: Confirms the UAE two-tier model the compliance demo assumes: AAOIFI adopted + HSA on top

rows.title: IFSB-10 Guiding Principles on Shari'ah Governance Systems
key_clauses: Principle 1.1: governance structure commensurate and proportionate with size, complexity, nature of business
Competence: measures for expertise, performance evaluation, professional development of Shari'ah boards
Independence defined: sound judgement without influence from management or outside interests
rows.supersession_note: joint IFSB-AAOIFI revised SG framework in final stage will supersede — watch item stands

rows.title: IFSB-17 Core Principles for Islamic Finance Regulation (Banking) — CPIFR
key_clauses: 33 core principles (CPIFR 1-33), mapped against Basel BCPs
CPIFR 16: Shari'ah governance framework as a supervisory requirement; CPIFR 32 covers Islamic windows

rows.title: IFSB-30 Revised Guiding Principles on Corporate Governance (Banking)
key_clauses: Revises IFSB-3 in light of post-GFC global regulatory change (stated in text)
Principle 1: board holds overall responsibility — strategy, governance framework, corporate culture

rows.title: SS 59 Sale of Debt
rows.issued: 29 December 2018 (22 Rabi' al-Akhirah 1440H); endorsed Shari'ah Board 65th meeting, Bahrain (verified in text)
key_clauses: 2 debt defined: established, owed asset — money, commodities or usufructs; from loan, commutative contract, or tort
4/1/1 sale of debt to the DEBTOR permitted subject to no-riba rules (currency substitution allowed at settlement-day rate, possession in session)
4/1/3/1 extinction of debt in debt (faskh al-dayn) prohibited — no new larger debt replacing the old
4/1/3/3 anything increasing debt amount against more time = prohibited (riba al-jahiliyyah pattern); 'inah form named
5/1 NOT permitted to sell a monetary debt to a third party for cash or another monetary debt
5/2 permitted against a spot commodity, or ascertained usufruct/service
8/2/2 combined-asset entities: tangibles must exceed 50% to trade freely
8/2/3 sukuk tradability floor: tangibles never below 33%, else notify holders + delist
9/1/2 discounting commercial papers not permitted (early-settlement rebate to first creditor allowed)
9/6/2 factoring on discount not permitted unless against commodity/ascertained usufruct or service
9/7 no swapping receivables portfolios between institutions
